newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Telcel plans $150 mln bond issue this yr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Telcel plans $150 mln bond issue this yr.

text.p: Venezuelan cellular telephone company Telcel, majority-owned by BellSouth, plans to issue $150 million in bonds this year to finance investments over the next three years, the company's president said.
"We are working on it. We are selecting an investment bank to do it before the end of this year," Oswaldo Cisneros told reporters in Congress.
BellSouth Corp owns 54 percent of Telcel and the family-owned Cisneros Group owns the remaining 46 percent.

Cisneros, in Congress to respond to accusations that cellular companies have signed up more customers than they can accommodate, said Telcel had invested $120 million up to July and would invest another $85 million by the end of the year.

Following a number of consumer complaints, telecommunications watchdog CONATEL last month ordered Telcel and GTE Corp's Movilnet to stop accepting new customers until they had expanded their networks.
Telcel has 463,000 subscribers in a market of about 700,000, Cisneros said.
Venezuela has the highest cellular telephone usage per capita in Latin America with 35 phones per 1,000 inhabitants.
